hypotheses.claim: The designed common RAMP slope itself is too steep
hypotheses.conclusion: REFUTED for the designed common RAMP (calculated); the recorded v(ramp) was not inspected
hypotheses.evidence: Ideal k x RAMP tracking slope at the -10 % RAMP capacitance is at most 0.3137 V/ms (+5) and 0.7611 V/ms (-12); the recorded peaks are 1.938x-3.044x the ideal and lie inside the low-voltage exception regions only.

hypotheses.claim: A start-order clamp release (U15/U16 on RAMP_P5/RAMP_M12 behind RCP1 1k) presents a fast reference-side edge to the +5/-12 trackers
hypotheses.evidence: Not tested: the per-rail references were not extracted from the recorded runs. The deck saves v(ramp); the per-rail reference nodes and their timing against the excursions are the next check.

hypotheses.claim: The excess is a maximum-step artefact
hypotheses.conclusion: REFUTED for maximum step; UNRESOLVED for other solver settings and macromodel accuracy
hypotheses.evidence: 5 us to 2 us changes the peak by +0.01034 % (+5) and +0.01040 % (-12); reltol/abstol/method and vendor-model fidelity were not varied for these cases.

hypotheses.claim: Slope and current exceedances are one constraint, not two
hypotheses.evidence: The recorded ESR-branch currents equal C x dV/dt at the peak within ESR effects (+5: 114.58 vs 114.51 mA; -12: 265.46 vs 265.26 mA), and each current ceiling corresponds to the slope ceiling at contract capacitance (114 mA / 120 uF = 0.95 V/ms against 0.95 V/ms (equal); 265 mA / 180 uF = 1.4722 V/ms against 1.47 V/ms (slope ceiling tighter)). For the modeled pure C + ESR load a correction must reduce the slope; a current-only argument cannot pass. A load with a resistive or nonlinear part would separate the two.

hypotheses.claim: No-load excursions come from the pair passing its pre-bias target near conduction onset with no load to pull the output back
hypotheses.evidence: Consistent with no-load-only occurrence and the low-voltage location, and with the phase-10 prose. Distinguishing it needs one paired run changing only the pre-bias target (RT12O/RT5O/RT12NO) or integrator CT on nom/adv, after design review. Not run.
Small negative adjacent-sample increments remain; no numerical tolerance is adopted.

assumptions: Ideal simultaneous disconnect at t = 0 (disconnect-before-discharge, AGND connected).
Discharge switch on-resistance omitted (it only lengthens decay).
Disconnect skew between the rails is taken as zero; the contract allows up to 1 ms and the installed skew is unbounded (see disconnect_order).
Loads are fixed resistors at the 20 ms transient minimum; the OSC load-versus-voltage characteristic is UNSOURCED.

'Absent' is not defined numerically by the contract; the cases use the rail discharge level (0.5 V) as a labelled assumption, add the contract's informal 'about 1.5 V', and the undefined case stays OPEN.
OSC +/-12 V loads are largely rail-to-rail, which couples the rails; one-rail-to-AGND loads are an illustrative assumption, not the OSC load.

disconnect_order.reason: Disconnect and discharge start from the same EN_E state with no designed ordering, through unequal paths: +12/+5 disconnect EN_E -> Q33 -> EN_N (REN 10k pull-up) -> Q10/Q11; -12 disconnect Q24 -> RG3A 56k -> Q25; discharge from the CDH hold-up: Q56 -> DIS_P (R60 100k pulldown) -> Q51/Q52, and Q54 -> R61 470k / R62 1M divider -> Q55. Relative timing needs device switching data and the CSD18543Q3A gate-charge path, which the decks omit. Overlap current is limited by the discharge resistors (above); that is a consequence, not compliance.

hypotheses.claim: At zero load the discharge resistors alone meet the level, time and voltage-form rows
hypotheses.conclusion: SUPPORTED only for absent <= 1.44 V with ideal simultaneous disconnect (calculated); disconnect order is D2-H3
hypotheses.evidence: All rails reach their discharge level inside 100 ms. With absent = 0.5 V there is no R-VEE, direct-hazard or screen event; R-VEE first fails at an absent threshold of 1.45 V, and at 1.5 V it fails (zero_load_absent_1_5v).

hypotheses.claim: Independent asymmetric loads can reorder decay into a forbidden state
hypotheses.conclusion: SUPPORTED under the stated resistive-load and absent-threshold assumptions; UNRESOLVED for the installed system
hypotheses.evidence: A loaded rail collapses in about 3 ms while the other still exceeds 10 V, giving R-VEE and direct-hazard events. Passive per-rail discharge does not couple the rails.

hypotheses.claim: Outputs are disconnected before active discharge begins
hypotheses.evidence: Same EN_E state, no designed ordering, unequal drive paths; switching data and an installed timing bound are missing.

hypotheses.claim: Trip thresholds inside the window establish the 2.1/2.0/0.5 A maximum
hypotheses.evidence: The limiter trips and opens; it does not regulate. Delivered current grows until switch-off, so the worst-case delivered peak is at least trip_max; trip_max is not an upper bound.

hypotheses.claim: Delivered current including overshoot stays within the contract maximum
hypotheses.evidence: Needs a guaranteed detection-to-switch-off time and a load-side di/dt bound. Margins are 15.15 / 4.56 / 39.16 mA (+12 / -12 / +5), so even a 1 us total response allows at most 4.56 mA/us of growth on -12.

next_inputs: D1: design review of one paired nom/adv run varying only the pre-bias target or integrator CT (distinguishes D1-H4); requires the hard-circuit review role before admission.
D2: OSC per-rail load current versus voltage during shutdown (or an agreed bound), a numeric definition of 'absent', and device switching data for the disconnect/discharge edge.
D3: a guaranteed detection-to-switch-off time and a load-side di/dt bound, or an explicitly agreed regulating current-limit change; no excess-current budget is adopted.
